summary: This Wikipedia-derived note profiles Prince Edward, Earl of Wessex, born 10 March 1964, the youngest of four children and third son of Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip. It covers his place in the line of succession, his work as a full-time working royal often alongside his wife, and his taking over of many duties from his father after the Duke of Edinburgh retired in 2017. It also notes his roles in the Commonwealth Games Federation and the Duke of Edinburgh's Award Scheme, and the Commonwealth Games he opened.
one_line: Biographical note on Prince Edward, Earl of Wessex, the youngest child of Queen Elizabeth II and his royal duties and Commonwealth Games roles.
key_facts: Prince Edward, Earl of Wessex, full name Edward Antony Richard Louis, was born on 10 March 1964.
Prince Edward is the youngest of four children and the third son of Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh.
At the time of his birth, Prince Edward was third in line of succession to the British throne.
The note states that Prince Edward is now 11th in line of succession to the British throne.
The Earl is a full-time working member of the British royal family who supports the Queen in her official duties.
Prince Edward often carries out official duties alongside his wife, the Countess of Wessex.
Prince Edward has assumed many duties from his father, the Duke of Edinburgh, who retired from public life in 2017.
Prince Edward succeeded Prince Philip as president of the Commonwealth Games Federation.
Prince Edward has been vice-patron of the Commonwealth Games Federation since 2006.
Prince Edward opened the 1990 Commonwealth Games in New Zealand.
Prince Edward opened the 1998 Commonwealth Games in Malaysia.
Prince Edward has taken over the Duke of Edinburgh's role in the Duke of Edinburgh's Award Scheme.
